claim: Air Liquide's Asia Pacific Electronics revenue grew 3.1% in 2025 (6.1% excluding Equipment & Installation sales), with carrier gases sales up more than 10% after seven new production units started in the first half of 2025.
evidence: Asia Pacific section: "Electronics revenue was up +3.1% in 2025, and +6.1% excluding Equipment & Installation sales. Carrier gases sales posted strong growth of more than +10%, supported by the start-up of seven new production units in the 1st half of 2025." (FY2025 PR + Activity Report, p. 13-14, Asia Pacific)

claim: JSR Corporation's shares were delisted from the Tokyo Stock Exchange on 25 June 2024, after shareholders approved a squeeze-out reverse stock split on 5 June 2024.
evidence: "At the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders held on June 5, 2024, the shareholders of JSR Corporation approved the proposal regarding the reverse stock split as originally proposed. We hereby announce that our common shares ... will be delisted as of June 25, 2024." (JSR notice, 24 June 2024)
notes: Completes CLM-1855 (tender offer result, 'scheduled to be delisted'). TSE/JPX notice of 5 June 2024 seen only as a search snippet, not cited.

claim: SUMCO management said in February 2026 that 300 mm long-term-agreement (LTA) wafer prices were by and large being respected and roughly flat, while SUMCO has few 200 mm LTAs, so 200 mm prices were softer.
evidence: "On prices, LTA prices are, by and large, being respected. So prices are not bad and are generally flattish. We don't have many 200-millimeter LTAs. So reflecting supply/demand, 200-millimeter prices were generally softer." (Mayuki Hashimoto, FY2025 results call, 10 Feb 2026, speaker segment before the Q1 outlook)
notes: Third-party transcript (tier 3). The passage the researcher could not extract (see CLM-1846 notes). 'LTA prices' is not tied explicitly to 300 mm in the sentence; the 300 mm link is from the contrast with 200 mm LTAs. SUMCO's own deck could not be opened.
